questions.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(9,10)=0.65,\,F(6,10)=0.31,\,F(3,10)=0.12,
$$

and the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{3,6,9,12\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Find $P(3<X\le 9,Y\le 10).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note the following:

- For a given joint PMF $f(x,y),$ we can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{3,6,9,12\}\times \{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Let's sketch the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/7790a013e37bb86c00b44b1c022d6597f9bbdd57616c48e7ee7dfe8ddf512c63.png)

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/379f0690fdbe92b7fb8f66cce4f12b214a23c6299fb8df71edf56d37fc0387fe.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained by taking all points in the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(9,10)$ (the blue region below) and *subtracting* all points in the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(3,10)$ (the red region below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/90a6730747b59a9886acbdf21880ca6a7ec3266142522ea5b32f07090963a98d.png)

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3<X\le 9,Y\le 10) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(9,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 9,Y\le 10)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(3,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 3,Y\le 10)}} \\  & =F(9,10)-F(3,10) \\  & =0.65-0.12 \\  & =0.53.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(7,1)=\frac{9}{16},\,F(7,-2)=\frac{1}{4},\,F(3,1)=\frac{1}{8},\,F(3,-2)=\frac{1}{16},
$$

and the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{1,3,5,7,9\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
$$

Find $P(5\le X\le 8,-1\le Y\le 1).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note the following:

- For a given joint PMF $f(x,y),$ we can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{1,3,5,7,9\}\times \{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
$$

Let's plot the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support, and sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/9ebff161899c6f61af3dffc1a5a0069de14bafd9b138293a945138e2951d066d.png)

Notice that this region encompasses the same possible support points as the rectangular region with its top-right corner at $(7,1)$ and bottom-left corner at $(3,-2)$ below, where the top and right boundaries are inclusive and the bottom and left boundaries are exclusive.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/e25278ed6d9712d8d2d2cabda5d1d0dbbf10aa8193f1342e7b4b66b26f9154e3.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(7,1).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(7,-2)$ and $(3,1).$

3\. Finally, we need to add back the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(3,-2).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(5\le X\le 8,-1\le Y\le 1) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(7,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 7,Y\le 1)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{bottom-right corner at }(7,-2)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 7,Y\le -2)}}-\overset{\text{top-left corner at }(3,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 3,Y\le 1)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{bottom-left corner at }(3,-2)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 3,Y\le -2)}} \\  & =F(7,1)-F(7,-2)-F(3,1)+F(3,-2) \\  & =\frac{9}{16}-\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{-1,0,1\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{1,2,3\}.
$$

Find an expression for the corresponding joint CDF when $x<-1,y>2.$
questions.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\sum }_{{x}_{i}\le x}{\sum }_{{y}_{i}\le y}f({x}_{i},{y}_{i}).
$$

Note the following:

- We can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{-1,0,1\}\times \{1,2,3\}.
$$

Let's sketch the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support. Let's also consider a point $(x,y)$ where $x<-1$ and $y>2,$ and a region $Δ$ that lies below and to the left of this point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/41e8a9d9ec73c9c10a73c4dcd8a8fe9051401d6ab31c8274fdf8f22adb2437da.png)

Since every value in the support of $X$ is at least $-1$ and $x<-1,$ no possible value of $X$ satisfies $X\le x.$ Therefore, there are no points in the joint support that lie in the region $Δ.$

Hence,

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)=0.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(9,10)=0.8,\,F(9,4)=0.3,\,F(6,10)=0.4,\,F(6,4)=0.2,
$$

and the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{3,6,9,12\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Find $P(6<X\le 9,4<Y\le 10).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note the following:

- For a given joint PMF $f(x,y),$ we can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{3,6,9,12\}\times \{2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
$$

Let's sketch the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/7790a013e37bb86c00b44b1c022d6597f9bbdd57616c48e7ee7dfe8ddf512c63.png)

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/6535c5bf152e8a9b09bf5522cdc442668add6c4cc7a0df4e07307f9931886a80.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(9,10).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(9,4)$ and $(6,10).$

3\. Finally, we need to add back the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(6,4).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6<X\le 9,4<Y\le 10) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(9,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 9,Y\le 10)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(9,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 9,Y\le 4)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(6,10)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 6,Y\le 10)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(6,4)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 6,Y\le 4)}} \\  & =F(9,10)-F(9,4)-F(6,10)+F(6,4) \\  & =0.8-0.3-0.4+0.2 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x,y),$ where

$$
F(4,1)=0.8,\,F(4,-1)=0.2,\,F(2,1)=0.3,\,F(2,-1)=0.1,
$$

and the supports of $X$ and $Y$, respectively, are

$$
{S}_{X}=\{1,2,3,4,5\},\,{S}_{Y}=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
$$

Find $P(3\le X<5,0\le Y<2).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note the following:

- For a given joint PMF $f(x,y),$ we can think of each point where $f(x,y)\ne 0$ as a point mass in the plane, where the "probability mass" at each point equals the probability associated with that point.

- The joint CDF $F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)$ is the total "probability mass" that lies in the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axis.

Given the supports of $X$ and $Y,$ the joint support $S$ is a subset of

$$
{S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y}=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\times \{-2,-1,0,1,2\}.
$$

Let's plot the points in ${S}_{X}\times {S}_{Y},$ which contains the joint support, and sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/6287f4884b335466bc7e1d6da17190f32d447f065e37a37e79a1aa48a6109415.png)

Notice that this region encompasses the same possible support points as the rectangular region with its top-right corner at $(4,1)$ and bottom-left corner at $(2,-1)$ below, where the top and right boundaries are inclusive and the bottom and left boundaries are exclusive.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14177883/assets/d4d76ca2e80bccda9cbcfa4e28c628dffcec62b3fb42d62f9315fce2623e12fe.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(4,1).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $(4,-1)$ and $(2,1).$

3\. Finally, we need to add back the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(2,-1).$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X<4,-1\le Y<1) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(4,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 4,Y\le 1)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(4,-1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 4,Y\le -1)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(2,1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 2,Y\le 1)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at }(2,-1)}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 2,Y\le -1)}} \\  & =F(4,1)-F(4,-1)-F(2,1)+F(2,-1) \\  & =0.8-0.2-0.3+0.1 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$
